statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail is 5 of 100 in the low band, twenty points below the 25-point block threshold, because the CME weekend closure removes the price path this score measures. Stress is 59 in the elevated band on a shut Saudi East-West pipeline, crude near 100 dollars, Houthi control of Yemen's Red Sea coast and a Wednesday policy decision priced near 86 percent for an increase. Confidence is 87 on a complete verified closing set.
recommendation: Tail sits deep in the low band, so the deterministic mapping returns EA_ON and a green status for both NQ futures and NAS100 CFD, and the single shared reading applies to each instrument. Two independent facts support it. First, Friday's completed path granted mean reversion rather than denying it: the Nasdaq-100 closed 29,368.44, up 264.93 points or 0.91%, yet finished about 105 points below its 29,473.12 high inside a 159.61-point cash range, while NQ futures traded down to 29,040.50 after the inflation print and recovered to settle 29,391.75, a round trip that retraced in both directions. Second, CME equity index futures halted at 21:00 UTC on Friday and do not reopen until 22:00 UTC on Sunday, about twenty hours after this horizon ends, so all twenty-four forecast slots describe a closed market in which a persistent no-retracement path cannot form. No evidence-based danger window is published, because a halted contract cannot define one. Stress remains elevated and is described here as an environment reading only: under the fixed repository mapping it does not alter the mapped state.
headline: A shut tape through the weekend: the Nasdaq-100 closed 29,368.44 and 0.91% higher but mid-range, NQ retraced a roughly 459-point round trip after firm core CPI, VIX fell 11.21% to 15.84, and an unresolved Saudi pipeline outage, Houthi control of Yemen's Red Sea coast and Monday's Oman meeting on Hormuz shipping all travel toward a Sunday reopen that lies beyond this window.
body:
Friday's price path is complete and it granted retracement. The Nasdaq-100 closed at 29,368.44, up 264.93 points or 0.91%, inside a 29,313.51 to 29,473.12 range against a 29,103.51 previous close, so the cash range spanned only 159.61 points and the close finished about 105 points below the high. NQ futures were wider and more instructive: a 29,040.50 low after the 12:30 UTC inflation print gave way to a 29,499.50 high and a 29,391.75 settle, a round trip in which mean reversion worked in both directions. The broader tape agreed, with the Dow up 0.98% to 52,573.30, the S&P 500 up 0.86% to 7,656.98 and the Nasdaq Composite up 0.96% to 26,333.04, each snapping a losing streak while still finishing the week lower. VIX fell 11.21% to 15.84, closing near the low of a 15.59 to 17.71 range.

The macro set behind that path is hawkish rather than disorderly. August CPI rose 0.4% on the month and 3.4% on the year, with core at 0.3% on the month, one tenth above consensus, and gasoline contributing more than a third of the monthly increase. Odds of a 25 basis point increase at the 16 September FOMC moved to roughly 86-87% from 72% a day earlier. The Michigan preliminary sentiment index then fell to 47.8 from 51.7, the second-lowest reading in the series, with year-ahead inflation expectations up to 4.6% from 4.0%. The H.15 curve shows the 2-year at 4.56%, the 10-year at 4.95% and the 30-year at 5.37%.

Energy and geopolitics remain the unresolved channel. WTI settled near $100.05, down 2.37% on the day but up about 9.7% on the week, with Brent near $104.61. Saudi Arabia shut its East-West pipeline, roughly seven million barrels per day of capacity that bypasses Hormuz, after drone attacks launched from Iraq, and has so far withheld retaliation while Baghdad investigates. Houthi forces are reported to control Yemen's Red Sea coast, and Gulf states and Iran are expected to meet in Oman on Monday on Hormuz shipping arrangements.

None of that can be priced inside this horizon. CME equity index futures halted at 21:00 UTC on Friday and reopen at 22:00 UTC on Sunday, about twenty hours after the last forecast slot. Every one of the twenty-four forward hours therefore describes a closed market, which is why conditional Tail stays in a single-digit floor that rises only gently, from 5 to 8, as unpriced weekend headline exposure accumulates, while Stress stays elevated at 59 to 61 on the environment rather than on any observed structure.

lookbackSummary: All twenty-four clock-hours from 03:00 UTC on 11 September to 02:00 UTC on 12 September carry a published Claude assessment, so every lookback slot is available and none is reconstructed. The window opens at Tail 11 to 12 in mixed mode through the Asian session, then firms into a trend-up read between 06:00 and 11:00 UTC with Tail between 13 and 15 as European hours extended the advance. The 12:30 UTC inflation print produced the only elevated readings of the window, Tail 21 and 22 in event/whipsaw mode with Confidence cut to 70 and 80 while the post-release path was still forming. Tail then fell back to 15 within ninety minutes as NQ retraced, held between 15 and 17 through the U.S. afternoon in mixed mode, and collapsed to 13 and then 7 around the 21:00 UTC halt. The final five slots sit at Tail 5 to 7 in normal mode, tracking the closure rather than a directional view, while Stress decayed steadily from 86 to 59 as the event passed and volatility fell.
outlookSummary: Every one of the twenty-four forward slots lies inside the CME weekend closure that began at 21:00 UTC on Friday, and the reference contract does not reopen until 22:00 UTC on Sunday, about twenty hours after this horizon ends. Conditional Tail opens at 5 in the current slot, the only slot containing observed rather than hypothetical structure, holds that residual floor through the early Saturday hours, then steps to 6 from 08:00 UTC, 7 from 14:00 UTC and 8 from 20:00 UTC as unpriced weekend headline exposure accumulates ahead of an eventual reopen. Every slot stays deep in the low band, so the deterministic mapping returns EA_ON and green throughout. Stress runs 59 to 61 and describes the environment rather than a path: a shut Saudi East-West pipeline with no restart date, crude near $100, Houthi control of Yemen's Red Sea coast, Monday's Oman meeting on Hormuz shipping and a Wednesday policy decision priced near 86 percent for an increase. Confidence decays gently from 87 to 79 as the verified evidence set ages without any live price path to refresh it. No danger window is published, because a halted contract cannot define one.
